Targeted unit tests for same-scheme non-default redirect ports and Response.is_permanent_redirect
test_stream_timeout and test_urllib3_pool_connection_closed pass without asserting when no exception is raised
body:
Two tests in `tests/test_requests.py` put their only assertion inside an `except` block, so they pass without checking anything when the exception is not raised.

**`TestTimeout.test_stream_timeout`**: if the request to `delay/10` completed without timing out, the test would pass. Switching it to `pytest.raises` (like `test_invalid_timeout` right below it) makes it fail in that case:

```python
def test_stream_timeout(self, httpbin):
    with pytest.raises(requests.exceptions.Timeout) as e:
        requests.get(httpbin("delay/10"), timeout=2.0)
    assert "Read timed out" in e.value.args[0].args[0]
```

I checked that this version passes as is and fails with `DID NOT RAISE` when pointed at `delay/0`. The change is in this commit on my fork, if it's useful: https://github.com/jeffev/requests/commit/b5058def5811

**`test_urllib3_pool_connection_closed`**: with the current urllib3, `s.get()` on an adapter mounted with `pool_connections=0, pool_maxsize=0` succeeds (I get a 200), so the `except ConnectionError` branch never runs and the test checks nothing. I'm not sure what behavior it should pin down now, so I didn't touch it.

I'd have opened a PR, but pull requests seem limited to collaborators.

title: ZIP extraction tests do not catch predictable temporary-file reuse
body:
The existing `TestExtractZippedPaths` cases pass against the implementation from before the fix for [CVE-2026-25645](https://github.com/psf/requests/security/advisories/GHSA-gc5v-m9x4-r6x2). They do not exercise a pre-existing file at the basename destination or extraction of same-named members from different archives. Current Requests already contains the fix; this report concerns the missing regression coverage.

## Expected Result

The extraction tests should catch reuse of a predictable temporary filename. Extracting a ZIP member should return its content without reusing or overwriting an unrelated existing file. Members with the same basename from different archives should retain separate paths and contents.

## Actual Result

The six existing extraction cases pass on the pre-fix revision `8b9bc8fc0f63be84602387913c4b689f19efd028`.

Two additional tests catch the regression. One creates an unrelated file at the old basename destination; the other extracts same-named members from two archives. Both fail on that pre-fix revision because extraction returns the reused path. All eight cases pass with the original fix, `66d21cb07bd6255b1280291c4fafb71803cdb3b7`, and on main at `3c7baaa05ab4aa49cc819ce3a819d260de19c157`.

## Reproduction Steps

The complete test-only change is in [openforge-live/requests@abf2080](https://github.com/openforge-live/requests/commit/abf208035425e39f59f56a9d12b43acdcfab5a66). It changes only `tests/test_utils.py`, uses small ZIP files in pytest temporary directories, and leaves production code unchanged.

Apply that commit to main at `3c7baaa`, then run:

```console
python -m pytest tests/test_utils.py::TestExtractZippedPaths
```

The expected result is eight passes. Running the same extraction test class against the pre-fix package produces two failures at the assertions that the returned paths must be distinct. The six existing cases still pass.

The prepared commit is linked here because this account cannot open a pull request under the repository's current collaborators-only PR setting.

## System Information

Verified on Linux with Python 3.13.13 and pytest 9.0.3, importing Requests from the source revisions above. The entire current `tests/test_utils.py` file passes: 218 passed, 13 skipped. The full integration suite, Windows and PyPy were not run.

title: Docs: link security vulnerability reports from CONTRIBUTING.md
body:
### Summary

The contributing guide explains how to file a good bug report, including providing a complete traceback and a small, reproducible example. It does not appear to direct readers reporting a security vulnerability to the private disclosure process described in the security policy.

Someone reading the contributing guide directly could mistake the public bug-report process for the right place to share vulnerability details.

### Relevant guidance

- [`.github/CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/psf/requests/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) describes the information expected in a good bug report.
- [`.github/SECURITY.md`](https://github.com/psf/requests/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md) asks reporters to use a private draft Security Advisory and says, “Please do not disclose this to anyone else.”

GitHub already surfaces the security policy when creating an issue, so this may not affect users who start from the issue form. A brief cross-reference in the contributing guide could also help people who arrive there directly.

### Suggested change

Add a short note near the bug-report guidance, for example:

> **Found a security vulnerability?** Please do not report it in a public issue. Follow our [security policy](https://github.com/psf/requests/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md) to report it privately.

Would a note like this be useful?

<!-- Summary. -->
In 2.34.0 `RequestsCookieJar` inherits from `http.cookiejar.CookieJar` (imported directly in `cookies.py`), while `merge_cookies` and other checks use `compat.cookielib.CookieJar`.
In 2.33.1 both used `compat.cookielib`. If `http.cookiejar` ends up loaded twice.

This is only reproducable under PyCharms Behave runner.
Works with 2.34.0 with plain behave in a terminal.
Works also with 2.33.1 with PyCharms Behave runner.

## Expected Result

No  "ValueError: You can only merge into CookieJar" using Pycharms behave runner with 2.34.0 or later.

## Actual Result

Running request in combination of Pycharms behave runner following error appears:


```
  File "<project>/adapters/api/rest_client/requests_rest_client.py", line 101, in _request
    prepared: PreparedRequest = self._session.prepare_request(request)
                                ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^
  File "<project>/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/requests/sessions.py", line 532, in prepare_request
    merge_cookies(RequestsCookieJar(), self.cookies), cookies
    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

    raise ValueError("You can only merge into CookieJar")

```


It seems that the behave runner is loading the package twice.
Ran following code at the failining line inside `prepare_request`:

```

jar = RequestsCookieJar()

```

Output:

```
('checked:', <class 'http.cookiejar.CookieJar'>, 'http.cookiejar', 50100923408)
```

Use requests inside a behave project. 
Start a test, which uses the problematic code via the pycharm runner.

Use the same `CookieJar` reference for the base class and the `isinstance` checks (e.g. use `CookieJar` in `merge_cookies`, `cookiejar_from_dict` callers and `RequestsCookieJar.update`, or inherit from `cookielib.CookieJar `again)

title: TestTimeout abandons three delay/10 requests and later tests wait out the server
body:
`TestTimeout` makes three requests to `httpbin("delay/10")` and abandons all of them:

- `tests/test_requests.py:2539`, `test_stream_timeout`, `timeout=2.0`
- `tests/test_requests.py:2573`, `test_read_timeout`, parametrized, `timeout=0.1` (two params)

The client raises at 2.0s and 0.1s, but the pytest-httpbin server keeps sleeping the full 10 seconds and serves requests serially. The next test that needs the server blocks until those sleeps finish.

```
$ pytest "tests/test_requests.py::TestTimeout::test_encoded_methods" -p no:randomly
1 passed in 0.56s

$ pytest "tests/test_requests.py::TestTimeout::test_read_timeout" \
         "tests/test_requests.py::TestTimeout::test_encoded_methods" \
         -p no:randomly --durations=5
19.79s call     tests/test_requests.py::TestTimeout::test_encoded_methods
 0.11s call     tests/test_requests.py::TestTimeout::test_read_timeout[timeout1]
 0.10s call     tests/test_requests.py::TestTimeout::test_read_timeout[timeout0]
3 passed in 20.55s
```

`test_encoded_methods` is one line (`requests.request(b"GET", httpbin("get"))`). The 19.79s is 2 x 10s of server sleep minus the 0.2s the two clients used. In a full run the cost lands on whichever tests happen to follow:

```
19.35s call     TestTimeout::test_encoded_methods
 8.00s call     TestTimeout::test_none_timeout[None]
```

Both call sites need the server to outlast the client timeout, not to sleep for 10 seconds. Lowering the delays leaves the assertions unchanged:

- line 2539, `delay/10` to `delay/3` (client timeout 2.0)
- line 2573, `delay/10` to `delay/1` (client timeout 0.1)

With that change, `TestTimeout` goes from 30.56s to 5.70s and the full suite from 167.44s to 142.04s, with the same results either way: 630 passed, 3 skipped, 1 xpassed. The single failure in both runs is `TestPreparingURLs::test_different_connection_pool_for_tls_settings_verify_bundle_unexpired_cert`, which is unrelated and fails before the change as well.

Measured at 611c616 on Windows 11, Python 3.14.2, pytest 9.1.1.

title: proxy_bypass_registry uses unanchored re.match (Windows proxy bypass)
body:
This was discussed here multiple times in the past so I'm opening it as a public bug report.

`src/requests/utils.py`, `proxy_bypass_registry` (main, 2.34.2):

```python
if re.match(test, host, re.I):   # start-anchored only
    return True
```

re.match anchors only the start, so ProxyOverride=google.com matches google.com.evil.com and bypasses the proxy for it — an attacker-influenced hostname can escape a proxy meant to inspect traffic.

Diverges from CPython: this is a copy of CPython's old code. CPython now matches with fnmatch (anchored both ends, wildcards preserved). Verified on 3.14:
- `fnmatch("google.com.evil.com", "google.com")` → False (requests returns True)
- `fnmatch("a.example.net", "*.example.net")` → True

Fix: use fnmatch(host, test) to match CPython, or minimally anchor: re.match(test + r"\Z", host, re.I).

title: Docstring examples in `from_key_val_list` show the pre-3.12 OrderedDict repr
body:
`src/requests/utils.py`'s `from_key_val_list` docstring shows:

    >>> from_key_val_list([('key', 'val')])
    OrderedDict([('key', 'val')])

Since Python 3.12, `collections.OrderedDict.__repr__` uses the regular dict form ([cpython gh-101446](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/101446)), so on any currently supported Python this actually prints:

    OrderedDict({'key': 'val'})

Reproducer (Python 3.13.5, requests 2.34.2):

```
>>> from requests.utils import from_key_val_list
>>> from_key_val_list([('key', 'val')])
OrderedDict({'key': 'val'})
>>> from_key_val_list({'key': 'val'})
OrderedDict({'key': 'val'})
```

The `ValueError` example in the same docstring is still accurate. Both stale occurrences are on lines 351 and 357, and a grep of the rest of the package found no others.

I have a two-line fix ready on a fork and would be glad to open a pull request if that's welcome. (The compare page says PRs are limited to collaborators, hence this issue.)

title: Encoding of escaped values in parameter?
body:
Hi,

I get a token from a server that's something like "FOO%3D". I need to return this token to the server as is, but when I set this value as a parameter to a URL, requests encodes the `%` as `%25`, so the string that gets sent is "FOO%253D". I see that there was an issue regarding this kind of thing (https://github.com/psf/requests/issues/5461) and it seems to have been resolved as to always encode the percent as if it were a literal, rather than part of the escaped value (%3D in my case).

Is there some decent way I can send the token as a parameter literally without requests trying to re-interpret what I've provided?

Thanks,

title: API-provided proxies are silently overridden by environment variables; no per-request opt-out
body:
Summary
Requests automatically uses environment proxies from HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, etc. There is currently no clean per-request way to disable this behavior. The only reliable workaround is to create a Session and set ```session.trust_env = False.```

Current behavior
When proxy-related environment variables are present, a simple request such as:
```
requests.get(url, proxies={})
```
still uses the environment proxy. Passing an empty proxies dict does not mean “disable all proxies”; it means “no API-level proxy was provided”, so environment proxies are merged in by Session.merge_environment_settings() when trust_env is True.

To actually bypass environment proxies, users must write:

```
session = requests.Session()
session.trust_env = False
session.get(url)
```
They cannot write:

```
requests.get(url, trust_env=False)
```
Expected behavior
I would like one of the following:
`proxies={}` (or explicit None values) to reliably disable all proxies for that request, including environment proxies; or`trust_env `to be accepted as a per-request argument, e.g. `requests.get(url, trust_env=False)`.

Why this matters
Simple scripts and library wrappers cannot easily switch to a Session.

CI / container environments often set `HTTP_PROXY `/ `HTTPS_PROXY `globally.

Some requests need to use the system proxy while others need to bypass it.

Forcing every caller to create and configure a Session adds unnecessary boilerplate.

Recent proxy-related changes, such as stricter proxy URL parsing in 2.32.0+, make this behavior more visible and harder to work around.

Workaround
Currently the only reliable workaround is:

```
session = requests.Session()
session.trust_env = False
response = session.get(url)
```
This works, but it is not convenient and cannot be applied directly to top-level requests.get() / requests.post() calls.

Proposed API
Allow `trust_env `to be passed per request:

```
requests.get(url, trust_env=False)
```
Alternatively, define `proxies={} `as an explicit opt-out from all environment proxies.

title: OpenSSL 4 removed built-in logic for SKID and AKID
body:
<!-- Summary. -->

The openssl command used to have built-in logic to automaticaly add
subjectKeyIdentifier and authorityKeyIdentifier to created certificates.
This logic vanished in OpenSSL 4.0 and the extensions are missing.
    
Python 3.13+ uses VERIFY_X509_STRICT to verify the certificate. Missing
those attributes is an error.

## Expected Result

A certificated with SKID and AKID.

## Actual Result

No SKID and AKID.

## Reproduction Steps

```
$ openssl version
OpenSSL 4.0.2 25 Aug 2026 (Library: OpenSSL 4.0.2 25 Aug 2026)
for cert in expired mtls valid/server ; do make -C  tests/certs/$cert clean all; done
pytest -v tests/test_requests.py
```
And then somewhere appears
```
 error = SSLError(SSLCertVerificationError(1, '[SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: Missing Authority Key Identifier (_ssl.c:1082)'))
 _pool = <urllib3.connectionpool.HTTPSConnectionPool object at 0x7f0a6d92a2c0>
 _stacktrace = <traceback object at 0x7f0a6dfa7a80>
....
 FAILED tests/test_requests.py::TestPreparingURLs::test_different_connection_pool_for_tls_settings_verify_bundle_unexpired_cert
```

I prepared https://github.com/sebastianas/requests/commit/339333739074118a93a9f496981b394e94bc1690 as a fix but can't open a pull request.

Sebastian

title: Proposed fix for #5888: preserve manually-set Proxy-Authorization on initial request
body:

title: Discrepancy in status_codes.py: 102 mapped to "early-hints" instead of 103
Drop the versionless `License ::` classifier now that `license` is a valid SPDX expression
body:
> This issue is part of a larger batch of similar-scoped issues we distribute in the context of our internal vulnerability and dependency tracking activities. The batch covers multiple projects, this is only one of them. The goal is to rise awareness and trigger/initiate the change towards clean project metadata in projects we depend on.

## Summary

This project already declares a valid SPDX license id/expression in its packaging metadata (`License: Apache-2.0` in the built METADATA), but the deprecated classifier `License :: OSI Approved :: Apache Software License` is still present. That classifier has no version and [PEP 639](https://peps.python.org/pep-0639/)-aware SBOM tooling like [cyclonedx-bom](https://pypi.org/project/cyclonedx-bom/) can't map it to an SPDX id, so it falls back to emitting the raw classifier text as a free-text license name. This free-text field is just noise and causes downstream tooling to flag this project as non-SPDX-compliant.

## Suggested fix

Remove the redundant `License :: OSI Approved :: Apache Software License` from `classifiers` in the packaging config. No change to the `license` field is needed.

## How to reproduce

```bash
uv tool install cyclonedx-bom
uv venv .venv-repro
uv pip install --python .venv-repro/bin/python requests
cyclonedx-py environment .venv-repro -o sbom.cdx.json
```

... and then check the `.licenses` property of the component. There should only something like:

```json
// This is how it should look like
...
    "license": {
        "acknowledgement": "declared",
        "id": "<VALID SPDX IDENTIFIER>"
    }
...
```

and _not_:

```json
// This is how it should not look like
...
    "license": {
       "acknowledgement": "declared",
       "name": "<CLASSIFIER TAKEN FROM METADATA"
    }
...
```

I'm happy to provide a PR to resolve this timely after approval!

title: SSRF: Unrestricted redirect following allows internal network access
body:
## Summary

get_redirect_target() and resolve_redirects() in sessions.py follow redirects to any URL without validating the target, allowing SSRF to internal IPs/cloud metadata endpoints.

## Vulnerability

Location: src/requests/sessions.py:134

No validation on redirect targets — can redirect to:
- localhost (127.0.0.0/8)
- RFC 1918 networks (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x)
- Cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254)

## Impact
- Internal network probing
- Cloud metadata exfiltration
- Access to internal services

## Fix
Add SSRF protection to redirect resolution:
- Validate redirect target host IP
- Block private/loopback/link-local/multicast IPs
- Add optional allow-list for trusted hosts

title: Cookies are not sent when the URL contains credentials
body:
`requests` extracts credentials embedded in a URL and sends them as an
`Authorization` header, but the same URL then matches no cookie in the jar, so
cookies are silently omitted.

## Expected Result

A cookie scoped to `127.0.0.1` is sent for `http://user:pw@127.0.0.1:PORT/`,
just as it is for `http://127.0.0.1:PORT/`. The userinfo component is not part
of the host (RFC 3986 §3.2), and cookie matching is on the host (RFC 6265).

## Actual Result

The `Authorization` header is sent, but `Cookie` is omitted:

```
without credentials  Authorization=None                  Cookie='sid=secret'
with credentials     Authorization='Basic dXNlcjpwdw=='  Cookie=None
```

The credentials are honoured for authentication, so the URL form is clearly
supported, but cookie matching on that same URL fails. No error or warning is
raised.

## Reproduction Steps

Run a local HTTP server that records the `Authorization` and `Cookie` request
headers it receives. Create a `Session` and set a cookie on it scoped to
`domain="127.0.0.1"`, `path="/"`. Issue two GETs against the server: one to
`http://127.0.0.1:PORT/`, and one to `http://user:pw@127.0.0.1:PORT/`. The

title: `HTTPError.response` is annotated `Response | None`, but is never `None`
body:
`HTTPError.response` is annotated `Response | None`, but cannot really be `None`. 
It's raised in one place (`raise HTTPError(http_error_msg, response=self)`) with a response bound.

I believe we could maybe narrow to  `response: Response` similarly to what was done in #7437

It used to pass when I was using `types-requests` which uses `response: Response | Any`. Dropping the stubs for 2.34.2 surfaced 22 of these issue in our codebase.

I'l be happy to submit a pr but it's locked currently.

## Expected Result

`e.response.status_code` type-checks under `except requests.HTTPError as e:`

## Actual Result

mypy: Item "None" of "Response | None" has no attribute "status_code"  [union-attr]



## Reproduction Steps

```python
import requests

try:
    requests.get("https://httpbin.org/status/404").raise_for_status()
except requests.HTTPError as e:
    print(e.response.status_code)  # union-attr
```

whether to immediately download the response default anwer=False, so it won't immediately download the response.         :param stream: (optional) Whether to use the streaming property. Defaults to ``False``.

title: MockResponse.getheaders does not return headers
body:
## Summary
The issue lies in: `src/requests/cookies.py`

`MockResponse.getheaders()` does not return the result of `self._headers.getheaders(name)`, causing it to always return `None`.

## Expected Result

`MockResponse.getheaders()` should return the value returned by the wrapped `HTTPMessage` object's `getheaders()` method.

For example:

```python
response.getheaders("Content-Type")
```

should return the corresponding header value.

## Actual Result
MockResponse.getheaders() always returns None because the return value is discarded.
Current implementation:
```python
def getheaders(self, name: str) -> Any:
    self._headers.getheaders(name)
```
It should be:
```python
def getheaders(self, name: str) -> Any:
    return self._headers.getheaders(name)
```

title: LookupDict does not implement full contract of the dict class
body:
## Problem Description

The `LookupDict` class in `src/requests/structures.py` subclasses `dict` but does not properly implement the full contract of the `dict` class. Specifically:

1. `__getitem__` and `__getattr__` methods read from `self.__dict__` (plain attribute storage) rather than the actual dict storage
2. All inherited `dict` methods (`__setitem__`, `keys()`, `values()`, `items()`, `get()` via the base class, `in`/`__contains__`, etc.) operate on the *actual* dict storage
3. This creates two disconnected stores, leading to inconsistent behavior

## Reproduction

```python
from requests.status_codes import codes
list(codes.keys())        # returns [] — should include e.g. 'ok', 'not_found', ...
codes["my_code"] = 700    # succeeds (writes to dict storage)
codes["my_code"]          # returns None — should return 700 (read comes from __dict__)
```

## Expected Behavior

1. `list(codes.keys())` should reflect the actual status-code attributes set by `status_codes.py`'s `_init()`
2. `codes["ok"]` (dict-style) and `codes.ok` (attribute-style) should return the same value and stay consistent after either form of assignment
3. Unknown keys should still return `None` via `__getitem__`/`.get()` rather than raising `KeyError` (this is an intentional deviation from plain `dict`)

## Root Cause

In `src/requests/structures.py`, `LookupDict.__getitem__` returns `self.__dict__.get(key, None)` instead of using the dict's own storage.

## Impact

This inconsistency breaks the expected behavior of dict-like objects and prevents users from accessing status codes through standard dict methods.

## Fix

The fix should ensure that `__getitem__` and `__getattr__` methods synchronize with the actual dict storage, maintaining consistency between attribute and dictionary access patterns.

title: raise FileNotFoundError for missing TLS material
body:
Would you accept a PR which changes the existing OSError for missing TLS material to FileNotFoundError?

e.g.:

```
            if conn.cert_file and not os.path.exists(conn.cert_file):
                raise OSError(
                    f"Could not find the TLS certificate file, "
                    f"invalid path: {conn.cert_file}"
                )
```

becomes something like:

```
            if conn.cert_file and not os.path.exists(conn.cert_file):
                from errno import ENOENT
                raise FileNotFoundError(
                    ENOENT,
                    "Could not find the TLS certificate file, invalid path",
                    str(conn.cert_file)
                )
```

Our use case is that there are temporary conditions where the files don't exist and it'd be nicer to handle FileNotFoundError specifically and be able to compare the .filename attribute rather than the more general OSError and test str(excp).endswith(...).  As FileNotFoundError is a subclass of OSError existing try/excepts continue to work but it would change the string representation:

```
>>> str(OSError("Could not find the TLS certificate file, invalid path: filename"))
'Could not find the TLS certificate file, invalid path: filename'
>>> str(FileNotFoundError(errno.ENOENT, "Could not find the TLS certificate file, invalid path", "filename"))
"[Errno 2] Could not find the TLS certificate file, invalid path: 'filename'"
```
